tsguard — TypeScript quality gate runner

Quality gates (replaces npm scripts):
  tsguard check          full quality gate + advisory maintainability/change
  tsguard fix            auto-format: ultracite fix
  tsguard lint           lint + format check (ultracite check)
  tsguard types          type checking (tsc --noEmit)
  tsguard typed-lint     native compiler-aware unsafe-operation and promise checks
  tsguard maintainability AST evidence for delegation and repeated error policy
  tsguard smells         focused maintainability diagnosis
  tsguard structure      runtime module graph, cycles, coupling and depth
  tsguard change         advisory Git baseline versus current maintainability
  tsguard complexity     compatibility alias; complexity is enforced by ultracite check
  tsguard fta            Halstead + cyclomatic + LOC score per file (fta command, default cap 60)
  tsguard coverage       run tests with coverage (vitest --coverage)
  tsguard security       security: secretlint + npm/pnpm audit + audit-ci + opengrep SAST
  tsguard npm-audit      dependency vulnerability scan (npm/pnpm/yarn audit + audit-ci)
  tsguard secrets        credential scan (secretlint)
  tsguard dead-code      detect unused exports/deps (knip)
  tsguard duplicates     detect copy-paste code (jscpd)
  tsguard criticality    informational: function/method caller ranking
  tsguard audit          informational: criticality + dead-code + duplicates

Environment setup:
  tsguard setup          npm install, configure AI tool hooks
  tsguard doctor         verify toolchain (read-only)
  tsguard hooks          generate AI tool hook configs

Flags:
  --output <mode>  human (default), agent (bounded), or json (complete result)
  --root <path>    explicit project root containing package.json
  --baseline <ref> explicit Git revision for source-only change comparison
  --dirs <d1,d2>    override target directories (default: . — project root)
  --exclude <d1,d2> additional directories to exclude from all scans (node_modules,dist,.next,build,coverage excluded by default)
  --timeout <s>     per-tool timeout in seconds (default: 300)
  --tail <n>        print only the last N lines of each tool's output to stdout
  --log-file <path> append full output to file (in addition to stdout)
  --if-typescript   only run check if stdin context indicates a .ts/.tsx file was edited
  --max-fta-score <n> FTA score cap per file (default: 60; >60 = Needs Improvement)
  --allow-pipe      suppress pipe refusal/warning (for CI wrappers that use tee)

Note: never pipe tsguard through an external tail (tsguard check 2>&1 | tail -50).
      Use tsguard check --tail 50 or tsguard check --log-file /tmp/tsguard.log --tail 50.
      In human mode, heavy gates (check, security, coverage) refuse to run when
      stdout is a pipe; use --allow-pipe to override.
      Lighter human commands warn on piped stdout but still run.
      Agent and JSON modes accept piped stdout.

response.quality_summary: In typescript-quality, tsguard types --dirs src --output agent exposed 12 blocking TS2322 findings and omitted two from its bounded display. The same invocation in JSON reviewed all 12 before editing. src/index.ts lines 1-12 assigned strings to declared numbers; these were changed to corresponding numeric literals while preserving numeric export annotations. The scoped types rerun passed, complete, exit 0, zero findings. The whole check --dirs src was rerun in agent and JSON modes: lint, FTA, types and typed-lint passed; FTA was 9.922897245213235 against cap 60. Overall check remained error/incomplete, exit 1, with three findings: no tests collected (invalid_configuration execution error), global lines coverage 0% < 80%, and global statements coverage 0% < 80% (two blocking quality findings). In that check, secrets, dependencies, security, maintainability, duplicates and change were not_run. Supplemental isolated maintainability and duplicates commands passed complete with zero findings. A supplemental scoped security run returned error/incomplete, exit 1: secrets passed; dependencies errored with partial normalization (adapter_failure and dependency_failure); security errored because bundled Opengrep is missing. Referenced dependency diagnostics show npm ENOLOCK and audit-ci inability to establish the package manager because no supported lockfile exists. These execution failures do not establish vulnerability findings or a successful SAST assessment. No dependencies were installed and no tests were added. The complete check is still not green; fixing the no-test/coverage configuration and provisioning security prerequisites requires work beyond the authorized typing repair. No baseline was invented for the quality project's unrun change gate.

dependency_review.explanation: A high-severity advisory affecting a devDependency is not automatically safe. With no valid explicit exposure review/policy, retain the native blocking policy and advisory visibility. A waiver requires evidence-backed development_tool or ci scope, product_exposure not_exposed, tooling_risk accepted, and manifest plus all existing supported lockfile SHA-256 bindings; classification alone cannot substitute for that review.

verification_reuse.explanation: The changed dependency lockfile invalidates equivalence with the prior green result even when source, tests and configuration match. Dependencies and toolchain/environment must also match. Rerun the checks applicable to the changed dependency inputs rather than claiming the prior result proves the current state or repeating unrelated checks.

unknown_status.explanation: A schema-1 result with unknown status unexpected is invalid evidence. Exit 0 and empty findings do not convert an unknown semantic status into passing or advisory success; preserve the original report and diagnostics for contract investigation.
